#include <yara/integers.h>
#include <yara/lexer.h>
#include <yara/sizedstr.h>
#include <yara/error.h>
#include <yara/mem.h>
#include <yara/strutils.h>

#include "grammar.h"

#define error(error_code) \
    { \
      compiler->last_result = error_code; \
      yyerror(yyscanner, compiler, NULL); \
    }

#define syntax_error(error_msg) \
    { \
      yr_compiler_set_error_extra_info(compiler, error_msg); \
      error(ERROR_SYNTAX_ERROR); \
    }

#define lex_check_space_ok(data, current_size, max_length) \
    if (strlen(data) + current_size >= max_length - 1) \
    { \
      yyerror(yyscanner, compiler, "out of space in lex_buf"); \
      yyterminate(); \
    }

#define yytext_to_buffer \
    { \
      char *yptr = yytext; \
      lex_check_space_ok(yptr, yyextra->lex_buf_len, LEX_BUF_SIZE); \
      while(*yptr) \
      { \
        *yyextra->lex_buf_ptr++ = *yptr++; \
        yyextra->lex_buf_len++; \
      } \
    }

#define alloc_sized_string(str, str_len) \
  SIZED_STRING* str = (SIZED_STRING*) yr_malloc( \
      str_len + sizeof(SIZED_STRING)); \
  if (str == NULL) \
  { \
    yyerror(yyscanner, compiler, "not enough memory"); \
    yyterminate(); \
  } \
  else \
  { \
    str->length = (uint32_t) (str_len); \
    str->flags = 0; \
  } \

commit 7e00915f1594b60fa19b39f29f77c046c99b14fe
Author: Victor M. Alvarez <vmalvarez@virustotal.com>
Date:   Thu Apr 21 17:33:10 2022 +0200

    Make fail_with_error() macro abort the parser on non-recoverable errors. (#1688)

    Until now this macro was aborting the parsing with YYERROR, independently of the kind of error. YYERROR aborts the parsing in a recoverable way, allowing the parsing to continue with the next rule. However, some errors like ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY may leave the compiler in an inconsistent state and we should not continue with the parsing.

 .github/workflows/build.yml |   4 +
 libyara/grammar.c           | 731 ++++++++++++++++++++++----------------------
 libyara/grammar.h           |   2 +-
 libyara/grammar.y           |  31 +-
 libyara/lexer.c             |  10 +-
 libyara/lexer.l             |  10 +-
 6 files changed, 407 insertions(+), 381 deletions(-)
=====
commit 7e00915f1594b60fa19b39f29f77c046c99b14fe
Author: Victor M. Alvarez <vmalvarez@virustotal.com>
Date:   Thu Apr 21 17:33:10 2022 +0200

    Make fail_with_error() macro abort the parser on non-recoverable errors. (#1688)

    Until now this macro was aborting the parsing with YYERROR, independently of the kind of error. YYERROR aborts the parsing in a recoverable way, allowing the parsing to continue with the next rule. However, some errors like ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY may leave the compiler in an inconsistent state and we should not continue with the parsing.

diff --git a/libyara/grammar.y b/libyara/grammar.y
index dc1384d3..6a8c5e4f 100644
--- a/libyara/grammar.y
+++ b/libyara/grammar.y
@@ -64,21 +64,36 @@ SOFTWARE, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGE.
 #define FOR_EXPRESSION_ANY  2
 #define FOR_EXPRESSION_NONE 3

+
+// fail_with_error() is used in parser actions for aborting the parsing with
+// an error. If the error is recoverable (like syntax errors), the parser will
+// report the error and continue parsing the next rule. If the error is a
+// fatal, non-recoverable error, the parser will be completely aborted.
 #define fail_with_error(e) \
     { \
       compiler->last_error = e; \
       yyerror(yyscanner, compiler, NULL); \
-      YYERROR; \
+      switch (e) \
+      { \
+      case ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY: \
+        YYABORT; \
+      default: \
+        YYERROR; \
+      } \
     }

-
+// fail_if_error() is used in parser actions for aborting the parsing if an
+// error has occurred. See fail_with_error for details.
 #define fail_if_error(e) \
     if (e != ERROR_SUCCESS) \
     { \
       fail_with_error(e); \
-    } \
+    }


+// check_type(expression, EXPRESSION_TYPE_INTEGER | EXPRESSION_TYPE_FLOAT) is
+// used to ensure that the type of "expression" is either integer or float,
+// the cleanup statements are executed if the condition is not met.
 #define check_type_with_cleanup(expression, expected_type, op, cleanup) \
     if (((expression.type) & (expected_type)) == 0) \
     { \
@@ -1806,9 +1821,8 @@ expression
         {
           yr_compiler_set_error_extra_info(
               compiler, "percentage must be between 1 and 100 (inclusive)");
-          compiler->last_error = ERROR_INVALID_PERCENTAGE;
-          yyerror(yyscanner, compiler, NULL);
-          YYERROR;
+
+          fail_with_error(ERROR_INVALID_PERCENTAGE);
         }

         yr_parser_emit_with_arg(yyscanner, OP_OF_PERCENT, OF_STRING_SET, NULL, NULL);
@@ -1826,9 +1840,8 @@ expression
         {
           yr_compiler_set_error_extra_info(
               compiler, "percentage must be between 1 and 100 (inclusive)");
-          compiler->last_error = ERROR_INVALID_PERCENTAGE;
-          yyerror(yyscanner, compiler, NULL);
-          YYERROR;
+
+          fail_with_error(ERROR_INVALID_PERCENTAGE);
         }

         yr_parser_emit_with_arg(yyscanner, OP_OF_PERCENT, OF_RULE_SET, NULL, NULL);

commit ce37922e2641e1be876a029a6b1020f919d52b8c
Author: Victor M. Alvarez <vmalvarez@virustotal.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 8 12:26:04 2017 +0100

    Revert to returning yyterminate() from the lexer when an error is found.

    This aborts the lexer, causing the parser to return a spurious "syntax error, unexpected $end", but if yyterminate() is not called it has other negative effects, as the parser continues executing while some tokens can have associated invalid data (for example an _IDENTIFIER_ token with a NULL c_string)

This is the key insight. The commit `ce37922e` reverts to calling `yyterminate()` in the `error` macro. The commit message says: "if yyterminate() is not called it has other negative effects, as the parser continues executing while some tokens can have associated invalid data (for example an _IDENTIFIER_ token with a NULL c_string)".

So the bug is: when the lexer encounters an error (e.g., `error(ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY)` or a syntax error), it sets `compiler->last_result` and calls `yyerror` but does NOT call `yyterminate()`. This means the lexer continues and returns tokens with invalid data (e.g., a NULL c_string). Then the parser processes these tokens and frees them, causing a double-free.

```
#define error(error_code) \

      compiler->last_result = error_code; \
      yyerror(yyscanner, compiler, NULL); \
    }
```

So in the current vulnerable version, the `error` macro does NOT call `yyterminate()`. This is the bug. When an error occurs in the lexer, it continues and returns tokens with invalid data.

But how does this cause a double-free? The commit message mentions "_IDENTIFIER_ token with a NULL c_string". Let me look at the `_IDENTIFIER_` token handling in the lexer.
